hints.title: Use unambiguous endpoint behaviour
hints.body: As x approaches 0 from above, (sinx)cosx approaches 0. As x approachesπ2 from below, (cosx)sinx approaches 0.
hints.recap: The two mixed powers can be identified at opposite ends.
hints.pitfall: The interval is open: use limiting behaviour, and do not assign a value to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>0</mn><mn>0</mn></msup></mrow></math>.
hints.pause: Which graphs approach 0 at the left and right ends?

recall.reminder: Know the sine and cosine values at the ends of a quarter-turn.

hints.title: Match endpoint patterns to curves
hints.body: Compare the endpoint behaviours you found with all four plotted curves. Keep the base and exponent in their original positions, and record which possible assignments those endpoint patterns permit.
hints.recap: Use the same endpoint and the same function when matching a limiting pattern to a graph.
hints.pitfall: A similar overall shape is not a substitute for comparing a specific plotted value or limit.
hints.pause: Make your endpoint-based assignments, then identify which curves still need an interior comparison.

recall.reminder: The base and exponent play different roles in a power.

hints.body: At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math>, evaluate <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>sin</mi><mi>x</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> using the exact sine value. Locate that height on the two remaining plotted graphs.
hints.recap: An exact interior value can distinguish graphs with similar endpoint behaviour.
hints.pitfall: Read the numerical vertical scale instead of relying only on the curve shape.
hints.pause: Identify the remaining two graphs and assemble the table row.

solution:
Near x=0, (sinx)cosx approaches 0, identifying Q. Near x=π2, (cosx)sinx approaches 0, identifying P. These are limits within the stated open interval, not evaluations of 00.

For the remaining functions, set x=π6. Then (sinx)sinx=(12)12=12≈0.71, matching S. Consequently (cosx)cosx is R.

In the order of the table’s columns, the graphs are R, S, P, Q: E.
